previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a morbidly obese male with a history of HLA-B27 positive ankylosing spondylitis, hypertension, asthma, obstructive sleep apnea, and anxiety, was admitted for a severe flare of left hip and cervical spine pain, along with bilateral lower extremity edema. He reported difficulty with daily activities and developed transient dyspnea en route to the hospital. Evaluation revealed no evidence of infection, pulmonary embolism, or cardiac ischemia. Pain was managed with IV and oral opioids, NSAIDs, and a left hip joint injection with Marcaine and Kenalog under fluoroscopic guidance, which provided partial relief. Edema was attributed to venous insufficiency rather than cardiac or renal causes. The patient was stabilized, transitioned back to home medications, and discharged with follow-up plans in rheumatology, pain psychology, and primary care. He expressed interest in using medical marijuana to taper off opioids and was counseled on gradual weaning.
problems: Ankylosing spondylitis of unspecified sites in spine
Morbid (severe) obesity due to excess calories

EXAMINATION:  CT C-SPINE W/O CONTRAST Q311 CT SPINE

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with ankylosing spondylitis, off therapies, with
SI pain and midback pain// Eval for etiology of pain      Eval for etiology of
pain

TECHNIQUE:  Non-contrast helical multidetector CT was performed. Soft tissue
and bone algorithm images were generated.  Coronal and sagittal reformations
were then constructed.

DOSE:  Acquisition sequence:
   1) Spiral Acquisition 13.9 s, 21.2 cm; CTDIvol = 29.0 mGy (Body) DLP =
577.0 mGy-cm.
   2) Spiral Acquisition 2.9 s, 4.7 cm; CTDIvol = 12.8 mGy (Body) DLP = 42.9
mGy-cm.
 Total DLP (Body) = 629 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  The cervical spine dated ___ and cervical spine
radiograph dated ___.

FINDINGS: 

Images are partially compromised secondary to beam hardening attenuation
artifact secondary to soft tissues and patient body habitus.  Bony detail is
compromised below C5 level.  There is mild loss of C5 height, stable since
prior.  Alignment is normal.  Subchondral cystic change along the inferior C3
endplate is similar, likely Schmorl's node.  No erosive changes of the
posterior elements.  No fracture or subluxation is identified.There are
multilevel mild degenerative changes, with mild endplate hypertrophic changes,
similar to prior.  Mild sclerosis of few anterior vertebral endplates may be
degenerative or secondary to ankylosing spondylitis, similar.  There is no
ankylosis of the vertebral bodies or posterior elements.  Central canal is
suboptimally seen.  There is no significant osseous encroachment on central
canal or foramina.  There is no prevertebral soft tissue swelling. There is no
evidence of infection or neoplasm.

The partially imaged bilateral lung apices are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:


1. No fracture or subluxation.
2. Multilevel degenerative changes of the cervical spine.
3. No evidence of ankylosis.  Mild sclerosis of few anterior vertebral
endplates may be degenerative or from ankylosing spondylitis.
